newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rejects labour, rights issues at WTO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rejects labour, rights issues at WTO.

text.p: Indonesia would oppose any declaration by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) that includes human rights and labour standards, the Jakarta Post daily said on Wednesday.

"Indonesia will reject the inclusion of social issues, such as human rights and labour standards because the discussion of such issues is not the responsibility of the WTO, but of the ILO (International Labour Organisation)," the newspaper quoted Industry and Trade Minister Tungky Ariwibowo as saying.
Ariwibowo will head the Indonesian delegation at the WTO's inaugural ministerial meeting in Singapore next week.

He said Indonesia would also reject a proposed multilateral investment policy because the proposal by some developed countries, including the United States and Japan, concerned matters which violated state sovereignty.
"We do need foreign investment. However, we should have the right to regulate it," Ariwibowo was quoted as saying.
He said Indonesia would also reject any inclusion regarding government procurement policies because state purchases were the prerogative of any sovereign state.
